_doc: Task 1628 — WHAT ARE THIS ENTRY'S FIELDS? ONE Python field grammar (library/scripts/_bib_parse.parse_fields; editor/scripts/bib_resolve.parse_fields delegates to it). Both silos answer `cases`: the library reads `entry` through parse_bib_text (library/scripts/tests/test_bib_field_parse_parity.py), the editor through bib_resolve.parse_fields (editor/scripts/tests/test_bib_field_parse_parity.py). `expect` is the exact field map; `app` records what the app's citation-js reading (src/lib/bib-parser.ts) shows for the same bytes where it differs or is notable.

cases.name: string-macro-kept-by-name
cases.app: citation-js EXPANDS the macro (journal 'Journal of Philosophy (n.s.)' given @string{jphil=...}); the Python grammar keeps the macro NAME verbatim, by design

cases.name: no-comma-between-fields
cases.app: citation-js REJECTS the entry (parse error); Python reads both fields rather than folding 'month = jan' into year

cases.name: inner-whitespace-preserved
cases.app: citation-js shows 'A long title' — the collapsed reading is _bib_parse.normalize_field_value, not the parse
